summary: Fisher Transform: median price turned into a sharp oscillator over 9 bars, with a one-bar trigger line.
overview: The Fisher Transform, by John Ehlers, turns price into a line with clear peaks and troughs. It plots in its own pane with a trigger line, which is the Fisher line from one bar earlier.
Colors follow direction: green while the Fisher line is above the trigger, red while below.
how: First, median price (high + low) / 2 is placed in its 9-bar high-low range and scaled to between -1 and +1, with some smoothing. Then Fisher = 0.5 x ln((1 + x) / (1 - x)), also smoothed with its prior value.
This stretches values near the edges, so turning points stand out.
use: Some traders watch the Fisher line crossing its trigger as a turn signal.
Use extreme readings as a sign a move is stretched.
Look at how sharp the peaks are to see how strong a swing was.
Pair it with a trend filter to avoid reading every swing.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It reacts fast and can give many turns in choppy markets.
